EduPhil Program. The EduPhil Program is hereby established as
the Government's national program for promoting the Philippines as a preferred
destination for international students seeking higher education, research, and
training in Philippine higher education institutions. The Progräm shall:
a. Promote Philippine higher education internationally by advancing academic
cooperation, research collaboration, innovation partnerships, knowledge
exchange, and the global engagement of Philippine higher education
institutions to attract international students and promote the Philippines as
a preferred destination for higher education;
b. Facilitate the entry, stay, and education of international students in the
Philippines through a modern, coordinated, streamlined, and digitally
enabled whole-of-government framework that improves the delivery of
government services, including the efficient processing of student visas and
related authorizations, consistent with existing laws and the statutory
mandates of the concerned agencies; and
c. Support Philippine higher education institutions in attracting and serving
international students, including through appropriate promotional,
informational, and facilitative initiatives consistent with the objectives of the
EduPhil Program.
The CHED shall serve as the lead implementing agency of the EduPhil

EduPhil Task Force. The IACFS established under EO No. 285
(s. 2000) is hereby renamed and reconstituted as the EduPhil Task Force, which
shall serve as the principal inter-agency coordinating body for the promotion,
facilitation, and development of the education of international students in Philippine
higher education institutions. The EduPhil Task Force shall be composed of the
heads of the following agencies:
Department of Foreign Affairs
: Bureau of Immigration
Department of Information and Communications Technology
Department of Tourism
National Intelligence Coordinating Agency
Professional Regulation Commission
The CHED shall also serve as the Secretariat of the Task Force and provide
the necessary technical and administrative support for the performance of its

The Task Force may invite representatives from national government agencies,
academic and research institutions, and other relevant stakeholders to participate in
its meetings as observers, resource speakers, or technical advisers.
The members of the Task Force may designate their respective alternates, with
ranks not lower than Assistant Secretary or its equivalent, who shall be fully
authorized to decide for or on their behalf

Responsibilities of the EduPhil Task Force. The EduPhil Task
Force shall exercise the following responsibilities:
a. Formulate policies and provide strategic direction for the implementation of
the EduPhil Program;
b. Develop and oversee the implementation of a five (5)-year international
education promotion strategy, which shall serve as the Government's
principal framework for advancing the education of international students in
Philippine higher education institutions, including the development and
promotion of the EduPhil brand as the Government's official identity for
international education promotion efforts;
c. Develop and oversee the implementation of the EduPhil Portal, which shall
serve as a single-window, interoperable digital platform to facilitate
documentation, endorsement tracking, reterral, reporting,
information-sharing, and the delivery of government services relating to the
education of international students in Philippine higher education
institutions;
d. Recommend legislative, administrative, and other measures to streamline
visa processing and related government services for international students,
improve inter-agency coordination, and address overlaps, gaps, and
inconsistencies in support of the EduPhil Program;
e. Recommend policies and initiatives to facilitate the reciprocal recognition of
academic degrees, qualifications, and credentials between the Philippines
and foreign jurisdictions, with due regard to applicable international
agreements and the respective legal and regulatory frameworks of the
concerned jurisdictions;
Constitute sub-committees and working groups, as may be necessary, to
support the effective implementation of this Order, subject to existing laws,
rules, and regulations;
g. Submit an annual report to the President, through the CHED Chairperson,
on the implementation of the EduPhil Program; and
h. Perform such other functions as may be directed by the President.

EduPhil Portal. The EduPhil Portal shall be established to facilitate
and streamline the delivery of government services relating to the education of
3

international students in Philippine higher education institutions. The Portal shall be a
secure, interoperable digital platform operating as the Government's single window
for serving as the unified point for international student documentation, institutional
endorsement tracking, and inter-agency referral, and as the Government's official
digital gateway for international student-related information and services.
The Portal shall serve as the common platform through which the member
agencies of the EduPhil Task Force, and such other government agencies as may be
involved in the implementation of the EduPhil Program, coordinate the exercise of
their respective statutory mandates and the processing of permits, clearances,
endorsements, certifications, visas, and other authorizations required under
applicable laws, rules, and regulations. Nothing in this Order shall be construed to
modify, diminish, or supersede the statutory powers and functions of any such
For this purpose, the EduPhil Task Force shall facilitate the execution of
appropriate data-sharing agreements and the secure integration of the relevant
digital services, databases, and information systems of the agencies referred to in
the preceding paragraph, subject to applicable laws, rules, regulations, cybersecurity
requirements, and existing agreements. All data processing within the Portal shall
comply with applicable laws, rules, and regulations governing data privacy,
cybersecurity, interoperability, and digital government.

Monitoring and Oversight. The CHED shall oversee and ensure
the effective implementation of the EduPhil Program. Within one (1) year from the
issuance of this Order, the CHED shall evaluate the implementation of the EduPhil
Program and, if warranted, submit to the President its recommendation on the
establishment of an appropriate organizational unit or office within the CHED to
support the effective and sustainable implementation of the Program, subject to
existing laws, rules, and regulations.

Convergence. All relevant government agencies are hereby
directed to render full support and assistance, as well as to actively coordinate and
cooperate with the CHED and the EduPhil Task Force to achieve a
whole-of-government approach in promoting and facilitating the education of
international students in Philippine higher education institutions.

Implementing Guidelines. Within one hundred twenty (120) days
from the effectivity of this Order, the EduPhil Task Force shall promulgate the
guidelines necessary for the effective implementation of this Order.

Transitory Provision. All records, pending matters, and existing
systems of the IACFS established under EO No. 285 (s. 2000) shall continue to be
administered by the EduPhil Task Force and shall be integrated into the EduPhil
Program and Portal, as may be necessary for the implementation of this Order. All
rules, regulations, guidelines, and other issuances promulgated by the lACFS shall
remain in force insofar as they are not inconsistent with this Order, until amended,
repealed, or superseded by the guidelines issued pursuant to this Order.

Funding. The initial funding required for the implementation of this
Order shall be charged against the current and available appropriations of the CHED
and other concerned agencies, subject to pertinent budgeting, accounting, and
auditing laws, rules, and regulations. Thereafter, the funding requirements necessary
for the continued implementation of this Order shall be included in the budget
proposals of the CHED and other concerned agencies, subject to the usual budget
preparation process.

Separability. If any section or part of this Order is declared
unconstitutional or invalid, the other sections or provisions not otherwise affected
shall remain in full force and effect.

Repeal. All issuances, orders, rules, and regulations, or parts
thereof, that are inconsistent with the provisions of this Order, are hereby repealed or
modified accordingly.

Effectivity. This Order shall take effect immediately upon its
publication in the Official Gazette or in any newspaper of general circulation.
DONE, in the City of Manila, this 8th
the year of our Lord, Two Thousand and Twenty-Six.
By the President:
